title: From Transformer to Vision Transformer (ViT)
reading: The slide introduces the Vision Transformer as a building block for vision foundation models, framing images as sequences of patches processed by a standard Transformer. The accompanying ViT architecture figure from Dosovitskiy et al. (ICLR 2021) is reproduced on the right, and the paper is cited at the bottom.

visuals.description: The canonical ViT architecture: an image is split into a 3x3 grid of patches, flattened and passed through a 'Linear Projection of Flattened Patches', producing tokens 1–9 plus an extra learnable [class] token at position 0, each combined with patch+position embeddings; these feed a Transformer Encoder, whose class-token output goes to an MLP Head predicting classes (Bird, Ball, Car, ...).
visuals.assertion: An image can be classified by a standard Transformer encoder applied to a sequence of linearly embedded patches with position embeddings and a prepended learnable class token.

concepts.name: Vision Transformer (ViT)
concepts.why_it_matters: Adapts the Transformer to images by tokenizing patches, underpinning vision foundation models.

concepts.name: Patch + position embedding
concepts.why_it_matters: Supplies token representations and spatial order to a permutation-invariant encoder.

concepts.name: [class] token
concepts.why_it_matters: Aggregates global image information for classification.

concepts.name: Transformer encoder
concepts.why_it_matters: Core self-attention backbone reused unchanged for vision.
